speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are an adolescent with delayed menarche, unusual physical features, and a history of bone fragility; to narrow this down, have you experienced frequent fractures from minor trauma, and what specific physical features have you or your family noticed?

speaker: Patient
text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. The patient's mother reports that during pregnancy she had abnormal hair growth on her chin. The patient has a history of severe acne and has sustained fractures following minor trauma. She is currently on oral isotretinoin and an oral contraceptive.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: 46,XX Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (due to 21-hydroxylase deficiency).

The combination of ambiguous genitalia (clitoromegaly/labial fusion) at birth, delayed puberty, and the maternal history of hirsutism strongly indicates an androgen-excess state from early in development, which has now progressed to suppress the HPG axis and cause delayed menarche.
